page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.4-64 is an x86_64 compute instance configured for environments that require an elevated memory-to-core ratio alongside predictable processor execution. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz, the server delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with two threads per core. It is equipped with 64 GB of total system RAM, establishing an allocation of 8 GB of memory per core. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Hardware allocation on this instance is fully dedicated, which prevents multi-tenant compute contention and provides stable runtime characteristics. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent data and system volumes. It also omits discrete GPU accelerators. From a resource-density perspective, pairing 64 GB of memory with an 8-vCPU footprint provides cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks that do not require massive parallel compute capacity, avoiding the need to over-provision vCPUs simply to acquire adequate RAM.

The hardware configuration of VM.Optimized3.Flex.4-64 is appropriate for in-memory caching solutions, operational databases, medium-sized analytics workloads, extract-transform-load (ETL) routines, and enterprise middleware. Applications that maintain substantial working datasets in memory, such as in-memory data grids and application servers, benefit directly from the balanced 8 GB per vCPU ratio.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.4-64 is an x86_64 virtual server designed for memory-intensive workloads requiring consistent processor execution. The instance runs on an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, supplying 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is provisioned with 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a high density of 8 GB per vCPU. The server lacks local storage and GPU hardware, depending on network storage for persistent filesystem needs. Dedicated vCPU allocation ensures steady computational throughput without noisy-neighbor degradation. This hardware configuration is well matched for in-memory databases, distributed caches, enterprise application servers, and memory-heavy backend processing pipelines.
